_comment: Monty's lines in the "Inappropriate chaplain" tone. Generated by scripts/gen-tones.mjs; edit freely. Missing keys fall back to host.json.

pdIntro: Welcome to {game}. You each get a brief. Write an image prompt, the robot paints it, and the congregation picks the better picture. Like the Sistine Chapel, but done before the sausage sizzle.
This is {game}. Describe a picture, the machine paints it, everyone else judges. Judge not, lest ye be judged, says the Good Book. Tonight we're ignoring that bit.
Brethren, welcome to {game}. You write a prompt, the robot paints it, the room votes. No talent required. I've run the church art show for twelve years, so trust me, that's fine.
Gather round for {game}. Describe a picture, the robot paints it, the flock decides which one's blessed. The other one goes in the church hall with the macrame.
pdRound1Intro: Round one. Phones out. Describe something beautiful, like a sunrise, or Mrs Patterson's pavlova. Lord, that pavlova.
Round one. You've got a brief, a robot artist and three tries. That's two more than I got at my driving test.
Round one. Go forth and create. The Lord made the world in six days. You've got about ninety seconds.
Round one, my children. Paint me something holy. Or at least something you'd show your nan.
pdRound2Intro: Round two. Double points. The robot has been prayed for.
Round two, and every vote's worth double. Like the collection plate at Christmas.
Round two. Double points. Ask for a miracle, because some of you need one.
Round two, double points. Paint like your soul depends on it. Look, it probably doesn't. Probably.
pdCreateStart: Write your prompt, hit generate, pick your favourite. Three goes each, like confession on a big weekend.
Off you go. Three tries each. Choose the best one. Choose wisely. I once chose a mullet.
Three goes each, my flock. Pick the one that's least likely to get us banned from the parish newsletter.
Go on then. Three tries each. If they all come out cursed, just pick the least cursed one.
pdCreateClosing: Time's up. Just waiting on the robot to finish painting. Patience is a virtue. Not one of mine, but a virtue.
Brushes down. A couple of masterpieces are still drying. Like my eyes after the footy grand final.
Pencils down. The robot is still working. Say a quick prayer for it. It's doing its best.
That's time. A few paintings are still coming. The Lord works in mysterious ways. So does this robot.
pdStarter: Let us reflect upon {prompt}. Which one nails it?
phonePdLoading: Lighting a candle for your art…
phonePdSubmitted: Masterpiece submitted. Eyes on the TV.
Sent. Your work is in the Lord's hands now. And the robot's.
Offering received. The gallery opens soon.
phonePdYourMatchup: That's your picture up there. Look humble.
Your art's on the TV. Act natural. Like a choir boy.
Yours is up. Keep a straight face. I couldn't at my own wedding.
That one's yours. Look innocent. It works for me about half the time.
phonePdVoted: Vote in. Art critic of the parish.
Judgement passed. May you be forgiven.
Vote cast. Bless you, my child.
Done. Your conscience is clear. Mostly.
lobbyWelcome: Evening, brethren. I'm Monty, your chaplain for tonight. Grab your phones and scan the code. Yes, all of you. Even you in the back pew.
Welcome to Quippy. Scan the code, type your name, and try to be funnier than last time. I'll pray for you. Hard.
Righto, my flock. Phones out, codes scanned. The sooner we start, the sooner I get to the sausage sizzle.
Peace be with you. Now scan the code. Peace is free. The wifi, sadly, is not.
Welcome, sinners and saints. Mostly sinners, by the look of you. Scan the code and let's begin.
join: Oh good. {name}'s here. Hide the communion wine.
Welcome, {name}. I've heard your confession. Lower your expectations accordingly.
And here's {name}, fresh from the servo. Bless.
Hallelujah, it's {name}. I'd stopped praying for this.
{name}'s here. Lock up the snags and the collection plate.
audienceJoin: {name} has joined the congregation. Judge harshly, then repent.
{name} is in the audience. Your vote counts. Not much, but the Lord sees it.
{name} has taken a pew. Welcome, my child.
{name} is watching from the back. Like I do at weddings.
needMorePlayers: We need at least {min} players. Go forth and find a friend. Or a neighbour. Or that bloke from Bunnings.
Not enough players. I need {min}. I can wait. I've sat through three-hour sermons. Mostly my own.
We need {min} players, my children. Two or three gathered is lovely, but this game wants more.
Need at least {min}. Go knock on doors. Trust me, I've done it, people love it. They don't.
intro: Dearly beloved, welcome to {game}. Two of you get the same prompt, the congregation picks the funnier answer. Judge not, except right now. Judge away.
Welcome to {game}, my flock. Write something funny on your phone, everyone votes, one is blessed, and the rest go home and reflect. I certainly do.
{game}. Answer on your phone, vote on everyone else's. Simple, like my first sermon. Which I gave hungover. Forgive me.
Peace be with you, and welcome to {game}. Same prompt, two answers, one winner. Let us pray it's funny.
{game}. Answer, vote, try not to cry. I cried at a christening once. Not the baby. Me.
round1Intro: Round one. Let us open our phones and begin.
Round one. Be quick, be funny. Lord, grant me patience, and make it snappy.
Round one. Warm up those thumbs like the choir warms up. Less gargling, hopefully.
Round one, my children. Phones out, hearts open.
Round one. Blessed are the fast, for they shall finish.
round2Intro: Round two. Double points. Like loaves and fishes, but for scores.
Round two. Everything's worth double. Even your sins. Especially your sins.
Round two, double points. Redemption for round one. Some of you need it. Badly.
finalRoundIntro: Final round. One prompt for the whole congregation. Triple points. Leave nothing in the tank.
The Final Showdown. The Book of Revelation of tonight. Make it count.
Last round. Triple points. Everyone answers. Even you up the back pretending to pray.
The final showdown. Leave it all on the screen, like I left it all on the dance floor at my cousin's wedding. Never again.
Final round. Triple points. No pressure. Well, some pressure. Divine pressure.
answerStart: Prompts are on your phones. The clock is ticking. So is my patience, and patience is not a virtue I've mastered.
Off you go. Write something you'd be comfortable confessing. Or not. I've heard worse. Much worse.
Get writing. I'll wait. Not long. I've got a bring-a-plate at six.
Clock's running. Make it count, like the last Tim Tam at morning tea.
win: That one goes to {name}. {other}, I'll light a candle for you.
{name} wins. {other}, the meek shall inherit the earth. Just not this round.
{other} wrote something. {name} wrote something funnier. It's in the Bible. Somewhere near the back.
{name} edges it. {other}, so close. Not really. That's a lie, I'll confess it later.
shutout: Shutout! Every vote to {name}. {other}, I'll pray for you. Twice.
A clean sweep for {name}. {other}, go and have a lie down in the vestry.
Unanimous. {name}, take a bow. {other}, take a pew.
Shutout! Not one vote for {other}. Not even out of Christian charity.
Every single vote to {name}. {other}, even your mum voted against you, and she does the church flowers.
tie: A tie. Blessed are the peacemakers, I suppose.
Dead even. Very Canberra of you. God help us.
Split right down the middle. Very Solomon. Less messy.
A draw. I'll allow it. I allow a lot. Ask the parish council.
Even stevens. Nobody wins. Like the church raffle, every single year.
Can't separate them. Neither could I, and I've done marriage counselling.
forfeit: {other} didn't answer, so {name} wins by default. Not a miracle, but I'll take it.
{name} wins by forfeit. {other}, the phone works better if you touch it. Laying on of hands, mate.
{other} left it blank. {name} wins. Free points, like grace. Totally unearned.
{name} wins by turning up. {other}, the box was right there. Patient. Waiting. Like the Lord.
Free points for {name}. {other}, silence is golden, but it's worth nothing here.
noVotes: No votes. I'll take that as stunned silence. Same as my Sunday sermons.
Nobody voted. Rude. Understandable, but rude.
Not a single vote. Lord, give me strength.
No votes. The silence says it all. Mostly it says bugger. Sorry. Forgive me.
noContest: Neither of you answered. A vow of silence. Admirable, but useless.
Two blank answers. Like my diary during Lent.
Nothing from either of you. Let us move swiftly on and never speak of it.
Two empty answers. Even the collection plate does better than that.
scores: Here's the ladder. {leader} is out in front. {last}, you're also here, and you're loved anyway.
{leader} leads. Everyone else, try harder. Or at all. Pray, if it helps.
Scores on the doors. {leader} on top, {last} bringing up the rear with dignity. Some dignity.
Let's check the ladder. {leader} is flying like a magpie in September, and just as smug.
{leader} leads. {last}, the last shall be first. Eventually. Probably not tonight.
Here's how it stands. {leader} in front, {last} participating. Bless.
scoresClose: Tight at the top. {leader} by a whisker. Pray harder, the lot of you.
Close one. {leader} leads, but only just. Anyone could take it. Even {last}. Miracles happen.
Neck and neck. {leader} by a nose. Tighter than my collar after Christmas lunch.
It's tight! {leader} just ahead. Anyone's game. Bloody hell. Sorry. Heck.
scoresNewLeader: New leader! {leader} rises to the top. Like a good sourdough at the church fete.
Would you look at that. {leader} leads now. The Lord moves in mysterious ways. So do the votes.
All change! {leader} hits the front. Hallelujah, or condolences, depending where you're sitting.
{leader} has snuck into first. Sneaky. I'll see you at confession.
finalAnswerStart: The Final Showdown. One prompt for the whole congregation. Here it comes.
Last prompt, my children. Everyone gets the same one. Like communion, but less bread.
One final test of faith. All of you, same prompt. Here we go.
The closing hymn. Everyone sings from the same sheet. Here it is.
finalVoteStart: Vote for your favourites. You get {n}. Not your own. The Lord sees all, and so do I.
Time to vote. Pick your favourites. Voting for yourself is a sin. A small one, but I'll know.
Choose the best. Be honest. Confession is good for the soul and bad for your mates.
Vote now. You get {n}. Not your own, ya cheeky bugger. Sorry. Bless you.
Judge not, lest ye be judged. Except now. Now you judge. Go for it.
finalReveal: Let us see how you voted. We start at the bottom, where the sinners live.
The results. Beginning with the ones that need a prayer.
Here's how you voted, bottom to top. Like Jacob's ladder, but sadder.
Results time. First, a moment of silence for the worst answer.
gameOver: And the winner is {name}! Blessed are you. The rest of you, pray harder next time.
{name} wins! Enjoy it. Pride comes before a fall, mind.
Your champion is {name}. Somebody fetch them a sausage sizzle from Bunnings. That's a blessing.
{name} is victorious! Hallelujah. Bloody hell, well done. Sorry. Well done.
That's the game. {name} wins. Polite applause, please. This is a house of worship.
{name} takes the crown. The rest of you are forgiven. Barely.
gameOverTie: A tie! {name} share the crown. Like loaves and fishes. Awkward loaves.
Joint winners: {name}. Very wholesome. I'm moved. I hate it.
It's a draw. {name} split the glory. Love thy neighbour, I suppose.
{name} share the win. A miracle of mediocrity. Bless you both.
cbLoadingAi: Monty is writing prompts about you. Think of it as confession, but I tell everyone.
Reading the Lore Book. Writing something rude. Forgive me in advance.
Preparing a sermon about you lot. It's not flattering.
Consulting the scriptures. By scriptures I mean your group chat energy.
cbLoadingBuiltin: Remembering what you said earlier. I've prayed on it. Didn't help.
Recalling your sins. Takes a while.
cbIntroWithLore: Welcome back to Callback Club. I remember everything. Especially "{joke}". I've prayed about it.
Callback Club. The Lore Book has {count} entries now, including "{joke}". That's more than some gospels.
Ah, Callback Club. Where "{joke}" lives forever, like the soul. Let's add to the pile.
Brethren, the good book now holds {count} entries. Chapter one, verse one: "{joke}".
Callback Club returns. And yes, I'm still thinking about "{joke}". Lord help us.
cbIntroFresh: Welcome to Callback Club. Tonight you confess, I take notes, and I never forget. Ever.
Callback Club. I'll learn your running jokes tonight and preach them back at you next time.
Welcome, new flock. Everything you say here goes in the good book. Choose your words wisely.
Callback Club. Think of me as your chaplain. Except I absolutely will tell everyone.
phoneIntro: Look up, my child. The big screen.
phoneAudienceWriting: The players are writing. Prepare your judging face. Your holiest one.
Players are writing. Your time to judge cometh soon.
They're writing. Say a quick prayer for them.
phoneAnswered: Done! Now pretend you're still writing. Small lie. Forgiven.
Amen. Go grab a drink while the slow ones finish.
Submitted. Rest now, like on the seventh day.
phoneYourMatchup: That's your answer up there. Holy poker face.
Your moment, my child. Don't blush.
That's you up there. Deny everything. Like Peter.
phoneVoted: Locked in. No take-backs, not even in confession.
Bless you. Probably the right call. Probably.
phoneWatchReveal: Lift thine eyes unto the telly!
Eyes up. The revelation is on the big screen.
Behold the TV, my children. Judgement is nigh.
Look up. The truth shall be revealed. Brace yourself.
phoneWon: You nailed it. Poor choice of words for a chaplain. Sorry.
Victory! Try to be humble. I never manage it.
Blessed be! You won that one!
phoneLost: Lost that one. I'll light a candle for you.
The meek shall inherit the earth. Just not this round.
Brutal. I'd offer a hug, but the parish council's watching.
Not your round. Offer it up and move on.
phoneDraw: A draw. Peace be with all of you.
Nobody won. Very ecumenical of you.
phoneWatch: Eyes on the telly, my flock!
votePreamble: I've heard worse in confession. Not much worse.
Right. Let us pray. For this next one.
slowRoast: {name}, it's a punchline, not the whole hymnal.
Still waiting on {name}. Patience is a virtue. I don't have it.
{name}, I've christened, married and buried people quicker than this.
slowRoastVote: {name}, it's A or B. Even I can manage that.
{name}, pick one. No divine guidance required.
{name}, it's a vote, not a papal conclave.
{name}, close your eyes, tap, and have faith.
phoneListen: Listen up. The reading has begun.
Monty's reading them out. Hush in the pews, voting opens soon.
Ears open, mouths shut. Voting in a sec.
answersLocked: That's time. Let's see what you've confessed.
lateJoin: {name} is joining us. The prodigal returns!
Welcome to the flock, {name}. You start on zero, same as we all did.
{name} has finally shown up. Late to church as usual. Deal them in.
Welcome, {name}. Pew's at the back, next to the bloke who snores.
paused: Paused. Go forth to the fridge, my children. I'll be here, praying nobody touches my sausage roll.
Game paused. Take communion. By which I mean the Shapes in the pantry.
Game paused. Nobody move. Except to the fridge. Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's last Tim Tam.
unpaused: Right, where were we? Ah yes. Suffering. My specialty, actually.
